headline: RBA rate hike expected next week as all Big Four banks align — plus crude oil crashes 6% and Middle East tensions escalate at the UN.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO slid 2.45% last night — no single major catalyst, but GTA VI launch timeline uncertainty continues to weigh on the stock. News that Rockstar is cracking down on unofficial GTA ports suggests the company is tightening IP control ahead of the big launch, but investors remain cautious about delays. Long-term thesis (GTA VI) is still intact — this is short-term noise.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dipped 0.96% today, continuing its weak run — down nearly 39% from your cost base. Lithium prices remain depressed globally as EV demand growth has slowed and supply remains elevated. No specific news today; it's a tough sector environment. The long-term case for lithium depends on EV adoption accelerating again.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 0.8% last night without a major news catalyst — likely some rotation out of large-cap tech. The long-term AI and cloud story remains very much intact; this is a minor pullback in the context of a strong year.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a solid session today, up 0.91%, likely helped by a rising AUD (which boosts the local value of foreign assets) and positive sentiment in Asian and emerging markets. A small but encouraging move.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.31% today, tracking the gains from last night's positive US session. The broad US market remains near record highs — good news for this holding.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG nudged up 0.21% last night — a quiet, steady session. Analyst coverage notes Google Cloud has hit $20B in revenue but some concerns around free cash flow. Overall the AI and cloud growth story keeps the stock well supported.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, up just 0.05%. As a broadly diversified fund, it moves slowly and steadily — exactly what you want from a core long-term holding. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI was unchanged today on the ASX. The AI sector broadly is in a news-heavy week (major antitrust lawsuit against OpenAI, Anthropic and Google), but no direct price impact on this ETF today. Hold steady.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike now expected next week — all Big Four banks agree
watch_today.detail: CBA, ANZ, NAB and Westpac have all now updated their forecasts to expect the RBA to raise interest rates at next week's meeting. If correct, that's a direct hit to mortgage holders — CBA estimates around a $1,464/year increase in repayments for the average borrower. Higher rates can also weigh on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on this — the decision is likely Tuesday or Wednesday next week.

watch_today.title: Crude oil crashes 6% — what it means for inflation
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil dropped from $100.30 to $93.91 last night — a fall of over 6% in a single session. Cheaper oil typically flows through to lower petrol prices within weeks, which is good for household budgets and could ease inflation pressures. If inflation softens faster than expected, the RBA may pause sooner. Worth watching.

watch_today.title: Take-Two (TTWO) — hold through the noise
watch_today.detail: TTWO fell 2.45% last night, adding to recent weakness and leaving you sitting at an 11.5% loss overall. There's no structural bad news — GTA VI is still coming, and Rockstar is actively protecting the IP. For a long-term holder, this dip doesn't change the thesis. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — patience required in a tough sector
watch_today.detail: PLS is down nearly 39% from your cost base and slipped another 0.96% today. The lithium sector globally is still in a downcycle — oversupply and softer EV demand are the culprits. There's no company-specific disaster here, just a tough market. For a long-term believer in EV transition, holding makes sense — but be prepared for more volatility.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI antitrust lawsuit worth monitoring
watch_today.detail: A major lawsuit has been filed alleging that OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI illegally agreed to slow down AI development. If this gains traction, it could create regulatory uncertainty across the AI sector — which would affect your GXAI ETF (a basket of AI-exposed companies). No immediate price impact today, but worth keeping an eye on as the case develops.

watch_today.title: MSFT — minor dip, long-term story unchanged
watch_today.detail: Microsoft slipped 0.8% last night with no major news. The AI and cloud business continues to grow strongly. For a long-term holder, this is just daily noise — nothing has changed about why you own it.

world.summary: The Middle East is the dominant global story this week — with Iran, the US, Saudi Arabia and Houthis all escalating tensions ahead of a key UN gathering. Meanwhile Trump is making major policy moves at home, oil has crashed, and California is pushing back against federal interference in elections.

stories.title: Middle East on the brink: Iran claims US is planning renewed bombing campaign
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has publicly claimed the US is planning to renew a bombing campaign in the Middle East, while the US is warning of 'rapid escalation' in the region. The Saudi-Houthi conflict is also intensifying, with Saudi Arabia's new defence pact now facing a major test. All of this is happening right as world leaders gather at the UN — meaning the diplomatic pressure cooker is about to get hotter. For everyday Australians, a wider Middle East conflict risks pushing oil prices back up sharply, reversing last night's crude price fall.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia's new defence pact faces its biggest test yet
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia recently signed a new defence pact, but the widening war in the Middle East — with Houthi attacks continuing and US-Iran tensions spiking — is putting it to the test almost immediately. If the pact holds, it could help stabilise the Gulf region. If it cracks, Saudi Arabia could be drawn deeper into conflict, which would have major implications for global oil supply and energy prices worldwide.

stories.title: Iran and Trump exchange fresh warnings ahead of UN General Assembly
stories.why_it_matters: The US and Iran are trading sharp warnings this week, with Saudi-Houthi fighting escalating at the same time world leaders converge on New York for the UN General Assembly. These moments — when diplomacy and military posturing happen simultaneously — can rapidly shift from words to actions. Oil markets are already volatile; a miscalculation could send prices soaring again within days.

stories.title: California's Newsom signs bills to block Trump interference in state elections
stories.why_it_matters: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed a package of election security bills specifically designed to stop the federal government — under President Trump — from interfering in state-run elections. This is a significant escalation of the ongoing power struggle between California and the Trump administration, and signals that US states are increasingly building legal walls against federal overreach. It's a story about the fracturing of US federal-state relations that will run well into 2027.

stories.title: Trump announces major policy moves: drug prices and Greenland
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump announced a fresh wave of major policy moves over the weekend, including action on US drug prices and renewed signals about Greenland. While details are still emerging, sweeping drug pricing changes would ripple through global pharmaceutical markets, and the Greenland push remains a wild card in US-Europe relations. These moves show Trump is still governing at a rapid, unpredictable pace — something markets are having to price in constantly.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was broadly positive — S&P 500 and NASDAQ both edged up — but the big story was crude oil cratering more than 6%, while gold slipped slightly. The ASX barely moved today. The Aussie dollar ticked up a touch.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Essentially flat today — the market is in wait-and-see mode ahead of next week's expected RBA rate decision.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: A quiet positive session last night — the broad US market held near record highs.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech led the gains last night, with the NASDAQ up 0.39%. AI and cloud stocks broadly supported.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: The big move of the day — oil crashed over 6% last night, falling from $100.30 to $93.91. Could mean cheaper petrol ahead, but Middle East tensions could reverse this quickly.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold slipped 0.85% — a minor pullback from very elevated levels. Still trading near all-time highs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly — traders are factoring in the expected RBA rate hike next week, which typically supports the currency.

politics.summary: The dominant domestic story is the imminent RBA rate hike, with all four major banks now aligned in their forecasts. The Coalition is also trying to score points on petrol prices, while Albanese is pushing for stronger AI regulation.

stories.title: All Big Four banks now predict RBA rate hike next week
stories.why_it_matters: CBA, ANZ, NAB and Westpac have all updated their forecasts to predict the RBA will raise interest rates next week. CBA's economists are warning borrowers to expect around a $1,464/year increase in repayments on an average mortgage. This is a major moment — when all four major banks agree, it's as close to a certainty as you get in economics. If you have a variable-rate mortgage, now is the time to double-check your budget.

stories.title: Coalition promises to cut $15 off a tank of petrol when global prices spike
stories.why_it_matters: The Coalition is promising to automatically cut $15 off a tank of petrol whenever global oil prices spike above a certain threshold — a cost-of-living play aimed at everyday drivers. It's a policy designed to contrast with Labor on household expenses. Whether it's economically sustainable is a debate for another day, but it's clearly aimed at voters feeling the pinch at the bowser — especially timely given oil's 6% drop last night makes the policy less immediately relevant.

stories.title: Albanese backs stronger AI regulation after meeting with Apple's Tim Cook
stories.why_it_matters: PM Albanese met with Apple CEO Tim Cook and came out backing stronger global AI regulation — including guardrails on how AI systems are developed and deployed. This puts Australia closer to the European approach and in contrast with the Trump administration, which is pushing for minimal AI rules. The government is also separately seeking big tech support for internet safety measures. Australia's tech regulation stance could affect how companies like Google and Microsoft operate here.

ai.summary: The biggest AI story of the week is a landmark antitrust lawsuit accusing OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI of secretly agreeing to slow down AI development — potentially to protect their own market positions. Meanwhile, Australia is pushing for stronger AI regulation.

stories.title: Bombshell lawsuit: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI accused of illegally slowing AI progress
stories.why_it_matters: A major antitrust lawsuit has been filed alleging that the world's biggest AI companies — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Elon Musk's SpaceXAI — secretly agreed to deliberately slow down AI development. The claim is that rather than competing as hard as they could, these companies coordinated to keep AI progress at a pace that suited their business interests and market positions, potentially squeezing out smaller rivals. If the lawsuit has legs, it could trigger major regulatory scrutiny of the entire AI industry — and directly affect companies like Google (which you hold via GOOG and GXAI.AX).

stories.title: Australia pushes for internet safety rules and AI regulation from big tech
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian government is asking major tech companies to cooperate on internet safety and AI regulation — seeking voluntary commitments before potentially legislating. This follows PM Albanese's meeting with Apple's Tim Cook and signals Australia wants to play a more active role in global AI governance. For everyday Australians, this could eventually mean stronger protections around AI-generated content, deepfakes, and data privacy.

stories.title: Albanese backs global AI guardrails as Trump vows to fight regulation
stories.why_it_matters: There's a clear split emerging in global AI policy: Australia and most of Europe want guardrails — rules about how AI can be used, what it must disclose, and how to prevent harm. The US under Trump is pushing hard against any regulation, arguing it will slow innovation. This divide matters because the companies building AI (Google, Microsoft, OpenAI) operate globally — whatever rules exist in the biggest markets will shape what AI can actually do for the rest of us.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 3 is heating up — controversial refereeing decisions, a big boilover, and Sam Walker firming to play for the Roosters on Friday. AFL season wraps up with Grand Final week madness and a Hawthorn controversy.

stories.title: NRL Finals boilover: THREE controversial referee calls spark outrage
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL Finals produced a major boilover this weekend, with the result sealed by three highly contentious refereeing calls — including what many are calling 'a penalty every day of the week.' The NRL is now investigating after a referee was pelted with rubbish by fans following the decisions. With the Dolphins hosting the Roosters at Suncorp this Friday, and the Panthers taking on the Knights Sunday, the finals are entering must-watch territory.

stories.title: Sam Walker firms for Roosters comeback ahead of Friday's final vs Dolphins
stories.why_it_matters: Roosters halfback Sam Walker has been training and is now firming to play in Friday night's Preliminary Final against the Dolphins at Suncorp Stadium. Walker's return would be a massive boost for the Roosters — he's their playmaker and general. Local Gold Coast fans will want to watch this one: Dolphins at home, Roosters coming in with a potential Walker miracle return. Kick-off is 7:50 PM Friday.

stories.title: AFL Finals: all-time classic finish rocks the competition
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL finals produced what commentators are calling one of the greatest finishes in recent memory. With Grand Final week approaching and AFL report cards dropping for every club, the footy conversation is at peak intensity. Airfares to Melbourne for the Grand Final have reportedly hit $6,000 — so if you're thinking of going, you've missed the boat on cheap tickets.

stories.title: Hawthorn players fined after ugly umpire incident — 6-year-old boy injured
stories.why_it_matters: Two Hawthorn players have been fined after an ugly incident involving an umpire during the AFL finals. The Hawthorn coach was forced to react publicly. More disturbingly, a 6-year-old boy was reportedly injured in the incident — the NRL also has its own crowd behaviour investigation running after a referee was pelted with rubbish this weekend. It's a rough week for footy officials across both codes.
